Snapshot

| Field | Contract |
|---|---|
| context | ProcessRef, optional run_id, input_snapshot_id/digest, contract_version, snapshot cursor and generated_at |
| inputs[] | Stable input/block/port ID, title, bounded value schema, unit/frame, required/default, provenance, dependencies, current value reference, configured option source and freshness |
| readiness | ready/blocked/unsupported, assessment identity/expiry, classifications and actionable reasons; check again at start |
| outputs[] | Existing EngineeringResult and representation references, roles/formats, exact producer revision/hash, assessments/currentness, supported view/download capabilities |
| interactions[] | Declared pending checkpoint ID/type/step, subject digest, frozen response schema or decisions, evidence references, state, instructions |
| actions[] | Stable action ID, operation, exact subject, enabled, reasons[], prerequisite references, idempotency requirements; backend authority |
| observations[] | Provider/operation identity, lifecycle/activity, nullable %/time/layer or generic metrics, observed_at, stale_after, provenance, limitations |
| diagnostics[] | Optional bounded recorded-run Reasons with owning step, correction and exact log/navigation references; no checkpoint or action authority |
| navigation[] | Validated process/block/run/result/assessment/evidence targets, no arbitrary executable URL |

Reason shape: code, readable_message, correction, affected_binding/step,
optional navigation and technical_details_ref. Default UI shows the message and
next action. Codes/digests/raw tool failures remain available in details.

Readiness classifications: supplied, explicit_default, upstream_produced,
declared_human_response, unresolved. Optional absent inputs are explicitly omitted.
Required unknown schemas/options/evidence do not pass. Provider option identity
contains configured binding+schema/resource revision+value; a friendly label is
not authority. A device-specific option shape stays provider data.

`waiting_human`, `waiting_external`, `reconciliation_required`, `failed` and
`cancellation_requested` have distinct visible meanings. A submitted action
receipt, observed operation start and observed completion are separate facts.

Scoped client

Public package `@wright/process-client` exports the same interface over two
transports: authenticated native Wright control plane and presentation-bound
preview origin. Host supplies scope; app arguments cannot select a principal or
another workspace. Public operation categories are:

| Method | Owner / behavior |
|---|---|
| getSnapshot() / follow(cursor) | Rebuild facts and attach events; no execution on subscription |
| setInputs(values,files,expectedSource) | Create/update preparation, validate schema and return snapshot identity; no accepted-source write |
| checkReadiness(inputSnapshot) | Compile supported dependencies and qualify current prerequisites |
| start(inputSnapshot,requestId) | Fresh readiness + durable start receipt + existing backend executor |
| attach(runId) | Server validates that run belongs to this allowed process/workspace |
| respond(checkpoint,subject,values,requestId) | Declared input response, frozen schema/currentness, one-shot continuation |
| decide(checkpoint,subject,decision,reason,requestId) | Existing exact-subject review authority; actor derived from auth |
| requestAction(actionId,subject,requestId) | Backend-permitted action only; fresh checks, consume/reconcile rules |
| cancel(runId,requestId) | Explicit supported cancellation; actual outcome, no success assumption |
| getRepresentation(ref) | Authorized bounded read/download; references resolved server-side |
| navigate(target) | Exact host navigation intent, not a process mutation |

No public `invokeTool`, `executeGraph`, arbitrary shell, destination override or
automatic approval operation is exposed to generated apps. A supported workflow
can still invoke its configured tools through the existing runtime.

Transport/API mapping

Under the existing authenticated workspace router mount, add a thin
`process-interfaces` API. Route suffixes below are relative to that mount; preserve
existing deployment prefix rather than introducing a competing API root.

| Route suffix | Operation |
|---|---|
| GET /process-interfaces/interaction | Snapshot for explicit accepted source reference and optional authorized run |
| POST /process-interfaces/inputs | Immutable prepared input snapshot |
| POST /process-interfaces/readiness | Fresh readiness assessment |
| POST /process-interfaces/runs | Backend-owned start; return 202 + run/receipt identity |
| GET /process-interfaces/runs/{run_id} | Snapshot/outcome reconciliation |
| GET /process-interfaces/runs/{run_id}/events | SSE following existing recorded events, with durable cursor |
| POST /process-interfaces/interactions/{checkpoint_id}/response | Input response; decision routes delegate to current review service |
| POST /process-interfaces/interactions/{checkpoint_id}/decision | Exact approval/artifact decision using current review owners; server-derived run and actor |
| POST /process-interfaces/actions/{action_id} | Exact permitted action; current services are composed, not reimplemented |
| POST /process-interfaces/runs/{run_id}/cancel | Explicit cancel request/outcome |
| POST /process-interfaces/inputs/upload | Bounded declared-file input publication; no preparation or execution |
| POST /process-interfaces/representations/read | Exact prepared-input or recorded-result membership and hash-checked bytes |
| POST /process-interfaces/navigation | Resolve exact presentation target through source/run/result/082 owners |

Existing result/validation/review read/export routes remain canonical. The client
maps to them through owning services. Legacy source-start stream can adapt to
start+follow for compatibility, but disconnect must no longer cancel execution.
Do not duplicate existing reviewer authorization or result repositories.

`PendingInteraction.decision` optionally exposes the retained decision, actor,
bounded redacted reason, request identity and integration-test attribution. It
cannot appear on input interactions. Native review bodies contain only the
source/session reference, subject digest, declared decision, reason and request
ID; actor, run, destination, automatic-review and integration flags are rejected.
The client verifies the exact returned subject/request/decision. Identical retries
read the existing decision and can repair an interrupted recorder projection;
they do not dispatch or rerun work. Approval consumption remains a separate action.

Native navigation returns shared `NavigationResolution(process, target,
representation?)`. The resolved target preserves every supplied identity and can
add its recorded producer/result identity. Run-backed result/assessment/evidence
navigation requires an explicit run; caller paths grant no read authority. A
checked result and its validator's recorded assessment file can have different
result IDs. Missing or ambiguous assessment files and omitted bounded-read
results remain unavailable rather than guessed. The workspace host retains open
editor drafts and observers while selecting the exact existing tab. This is a
presentation read, never a process mutation or action authority.

Generated apps access the same bounded operation envelopes under the reserved
preview route `/__wright/process`; this server resolves process/UI/run scope
from the presentation. Parent bearer tokens and printer credentials never appear
in app JavaScript. SSE reconnect uses cursor replay; a lost/expired cursor obtains
a full snapshot. Backend events are retained authority, browser state is cache.

For managed navigation only, the bridge supplies its authorized presentation run
when the target omits `run_id`. Explicit run selectors must match that binding;
they are never replaced. A preparation presentation supplies no run. The native
navigation owner still requires an explicit run for recorded output evidence and
verifies exact source/result/assessment membership before resolving it.

Representation reads accept optional `preview: "toolpaths"` and a confined
`archive_entry` only in that mode. They retain the same process/results grant,
exact run or preparation membership and original artifact SHA-256. The passive
derived MIME is `application/vnd.wright.toolpaths+json`, with view format
`wright.gcode.toolpaths.v1`; the SHA-256 response header identifies the original
recorded artifact rather than claiming the JSON bytes are the artifact.
Parser provenance separately identifies the actual G-code entry bytes and
records true layers, comment-based feature categories, nominal arc approximation
and excluded unlayered extrusion. Unknown labels stay unclassified. Multi-plate
ambiguity, unsupported motion, bounds or deadline return inspection/download
fallback; they never change process acceptance or dispatch any operation.

Currentness, limits and errors

Each mutation includes request_id, expected_source_digest and exact subject/input
identity as appropriate. Reuse with different payload returns conflict; duplicates
return recorded outcome. Cursor is for reconciliation, not permission to act.
Backend rereads current dependencies before mutation. A layout/theme-only update
does not alter engineering subject identity.

Initial bounds: 256 projected bindings/interactions per snapshot page, 64 KiB
inline value/diagnostic payload, 32 MiB image/file upload per item and 64 MiB per
input request; larger supported artifact representations use streamed vault
references and reader-specific bounds. JSON schemas allow bounded objects/arrays,
primitive enums/ranges/local definitions; no remote references/executable validators.
Required unsupported schema features return unsupported, not weakened validation.

Error categories: INPUT_REQUIRED, READINESS_UNSUPPORTED, SOURCE_CHANGED,
SUBJECT_STALE, OPTION_STALE, INTERACTION_NOT_DECLARED, RESPONSE_INVALID,
REQUEST_CONFLICT, CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, ACTION_NOT_PERMITTED, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN,
UI_INCOMPATIBLE, SCOPE_DENIED, PRESENTATION_EXPIRED. These are platform error
semantics; adapters map existing detailed codes without losing diagnostics.

Required negative fixtures cover stale source/result/option, absent required
evidence, revoked presentation, cross-workspace/run/UI scope, duplicate/lost
responses, and unauthorized mutations. Common and generated views receive the
same reasons. Unknown external outcomes block repeat submission.

Immutable input overlay v1

`wright.process-input-snapshot/1` pins ProcessRef plus typed input bindings,
explicit-default resolution, authorized file/representation digests and configured
provider choice revisions. A snapshot is prepared, then frozen before dispatch.
Preparation/execution/continuation read it through the same conversion layer.
Preserve source-defined inputs as defaults for legacy requests; UI overrides are
run values, not source edits. Ambiguous or incompatible conversions are rejected.

Extend accepted input settings with optional `interaction_input` metadata:
version=1, bounded value_schema, unit/frame, required, explicit default,
configured option-source binding and dependency selectors. Existing source stays
readable with inferred text/file types; inference cannot invent engineering values.
Schema UI labels and units do not silently alter tool arguments.

Before start, classify every reachable required binding on the compiler's supported
data/order graph. Upstream production is valid only when its declared output and
consumer types align. A declared human response is valid only from the pinned
interaction step. Unsupported conditional reachability is an actionable unsupported
readiness result. Recheck schema/provider/file/source identity immediately before
dispatch; no frontend readiness badge grants permission.

Explicit run-path binding v1

A reusable accepted process can declare `settings.run_path_template =
"wright.run-path/1"` on individual tasks and configuration-text inputs. The only
supported token is `{{wright.run_id}}`. Example saved/expected output:
`outputs/{{wright.run_id}}/report.json`. The token must be exactly one standalone
directory component before a declared output filename. Resolved paths retain the
existing workspace path checks; backend run IDs are bounded safe components.
Unsupported versions, unknown Wright tokens and templated object keys fail.

The existing authorized preparation owner chooses the run ID before tool
qualification. It resolves only declared task prompt/guidance, MCP arguments,
saved/expected output paths, expected-file port mappings and file dependencies.
Explicitly declared text inputs are resolved through the existing immutable-input
conversion before connected-argument schema validation. Undeclared input text
remains literal. Approval destinations, validation profiles, human-interaction
schemas and native application/document configuration are not template fields.
Reserved Wright tokens in those configuration dictionaries are rejected on every
step, including undeclared steps and processes with no run-path declarations.
They cannot remain literal until a later approval or document operation fails.
This is a bounded path binding, not an expression or execution language.

The accepted source, step/port IDs and frozen raw input snapshot are unchanged by
binding. File-template bytes are never rewritten: the reference retains its
original path, byte count and SHA-256 and separately records the run ID and
resolved-content SHA-256. Checkpoint identities bind both original and resolved
identities. Review/prompt context exposes the distinction. The resolved text
must fit the consuming step's inline budget; falling back to reading the raw
template file would lose the run binding and is rejected. Opaque file/native
imports and supplied-artifact approvals cannot consume a text template as though
its original file held the resolved content.

Readiness performs no directory reservation or engineering call. After a durable
start is accepted, the canonical executor exclusively reserves the declared run
directories before model/tool execution. An existing target blocks execution
rather than replacing its bytes. A resumed input/review checkpoint prepares with
its original run ID and requires the retained directory. Changed source/template
identity or uncertain execution still follows existing continuation/replay rules.
Legacy processes without declarations preserve their original behavior.

An external-action approval may declare one `workspace_file` output whose key
ends in `receipt`, `run_path_template: "wright.run-path/1"`, and a JSON
`output_filename` such as `outputs/{{wright.run_id}}/submission.json`. It must
omit `approval_settings.receipt_path`; simultaneous declarations conflict.
Local reviews cannot declare these receipt outputs. The compiler records the
expected file, and preparation binds its concrete path into the existing
approval settings before checkpoint identity, enrollment and dispatch checks.
No approval dictionary is templated. The existing dispatcher writes and verifies
the receipt; the model-response writer does not write an approval's response
over it. Same-run continuation uses the original concrete receipt, while another
run gets a separate subject and output directory. Legacy literal receipts keep
their existing behavior, and output-boundary/replay/unknown-outcome rules remain.

Source validator idempotency binds the durable run ID, validator step and revision.
Two runs of the same accepted source in one workspace receive separate attempts
for their exact output subjects. Retrying an identical retained request still
returns its existing assessment; changed input under that same key still conflicts.
Historical request/attempt records are not rewritten.

Every provider write must be explicitly bound and qualified. Declaring one
output does not isolate unmodified absolute paths, provider job names, native
documents, internal caches or other undeclared writes. This mechanism is not a
provider filesystem sandbox. Example migration must account for all writable
subjects and supported provider operations without vendor-specific rewrites in
Wright. A changed accepted source needs normal UI binding/compatibility checks;
only subsequent runs of that same accepted source can prove saved-interface
reuse. Current controlled runtime tests do not establish live provider or
engineering-interface repeat-run acceptance.

Human-input source extension v1

Use the existing task/settings source representation; add an explicit template:

```text
settings.authoring_template = "human-input"
settings.human_interaction = {
  "version": 1,
  "kind": "input",
  "instructions": "Choose the comparison to carry forward.",
  "response_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"selection": {"type": "string", "enum": ["a", "b"]}},
    "required": ["selection"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "output_port": "response"
}
performed_by = "engineer"
```

This is a semantic settings illustration, not a new source-language parser. The
actual `.wflow` fields remain the existing indented, JSON-valued source grammar.
Implementation must round-trip this declaration through canonical source/diagram
serialization and declare a typed output port consumed by downstream steps.

Compiler validates one response output, bounded nonexecutable schema, connected
upstream evidence and declaration compatibility. It does not create checkpoints
because an LLM asks a question. At the declared cursor the existing executor
records a barrier with exact source, input snapshot, upstream digests, schema and
checkpoint identity. No downstream execution is released before a valid response.

Response submission validates the frozen schema/subject and server-derived actor,
persists immutable values and one-shot claim, records an EngineeringResult at the
declared port, and resumes the same run. Declining/cancelling is explicit policy;
there is no forced answer. Two simultaneous submissions cannot resume twice.

Existing review/validation/external-action checkpoints retain their own decisions,
subjects and evidence. Do not turn input responses into approval receipts or
combine independent approvals under a single checkbox.

Scoped review requests retain `decision_receipt` in the existing approval
continuation JSON, atomically with its pending-to-decision transition. Terminal
artifact reviews retain their request ID in the existing immutable decision JSON.
No additional decision database or lifecycle engine is introduced. Actor and run
are derived from the authorized process scope and recorded checkpoint. Changed
requests conflict; the same request can reconcile a lost run projection write.
The recorder projects terminal artifact approval/changes-requested outcomes and
retains their exact review event. Review acceptance does not dispatch an external
operation. Older decisions without request metadata preserve their history shape.

Continuation and source compatibility

Continuation v3 adds checkpoint_kind (approval/input), input_snapshot_id/digest,
response_id/digest and compatible execution state. Existing v2 approval records
remain readable and resumable under their original checks. Changed accepted source,
upstream subject, required input or profile invalidates continuation; UI labels
and layout alone do not.

Do not relax the existing compiler's supported DAG/rework scope or port checks.
Invalid drafts never replace accepted source. Add editor controls for input schema
and declared interaction without replacing the refined canvas/inspectors.

Backend-owned lifecycle

Native approved action requests are supervised on the same recorded run through
the existing approval executor and consume authority. Persist the exact request
and authenticated principal before provider dispatch. Observer detach does not
cancel the owner. The response may acknowledge authorization before provider
acceptance: `PendingInteraction.action_receipt` retains the separate submission,
delivery, observed outcome and cancellation evidence. Unknown consumed operations
and unfinished continuation claims cannot be replayed; confirmed delivery with
no downstream claim may continue without re-dispatch. Interrupted claims are
sealed as outcome_unknown before final recorder publication. A matching finished
retry is read-only. Browser-cached intent is for explicit reconciliation only,
scoped to the exact process revision/run; it does not grant action authority.

One source-run use case handles readiness, input snapshot, durable start receipt,
run allocation and execution task ownership. It invokes existing
`execute_prompt_workflow`, gateway, recorder, approval/rework and async-operation
machinery. Start/follow are separate; observer disconnect cancels only observation.

The supervisor is local to the existing runtime, bounded and lease-aware. It is
not a new graph scheduler. Persist enough identity before tool dispatch to
reconcile lost acknowledgements. Backend death marks uncertain active segments
interrupted; reconstruction of waiting/finished state does not imply replay is safe.

Keep model/tool-call timeouts finite. Multi-hour supported external operations
use `workflow_async_operations.py` identities, read-only status/results and declared
poll/deadline/cancel policy. Do not extend a model call into an unlimited print monitor.
Absent remaining-time/% data is null; observed_at and stale_after are visible.

Runtime AI outcome is completed/blocked/error. An undeclared request for more user
information becomes an `INTERACTION_NOT_DECLARED` diagnostic with owning step and
correction, following configured failure/recovery policy. Never ask it as an
opportunistic runtime form or invent an engineering assumption to continue.

The configured tool-free model adapter uses the closed
`wright.unattended-step/1` outcome from `core.workflow_step_outcomes`:
version, status (completed/blocked/error), response (document string), and reason
(null for completed; input_required/capability_unavailable/execution_failed for
blocked/error). This disposition is separate from the requested document format.
The adapter preserves usage and disposition metadata on its existing string
response; execution checks it before saving, publishing or releasing downstream
work. A bare prose response or invalid envelope produces MODEL_OUTCOME_INVALID.
Legacy trusted injected string callbacks remain usable; they are not evidence
that a new external model adapter has qualified this contract.

Existing MCP task evidence envelopes retain their successful tool-call numbers.
Missing user dependencies use blocked + reason=input_required. A mixed
blocked/question-and-tool decision cannot dispatch its tool call; a formatting
repair cannot add an input request or replay an engineering operation. Questions
inside legitimate engineering documents are not classified by prose heuristics.
Recorded failures are optional bounded diagnostics[] in the shared interaction
projection, with correction, exact owning step and canonical log reference.

Neutral permitted MCP action

Add a bounded `mcp-operation` kind to the existing approved action dispatcher.
Its frozen subject contains exact configured server/tool/schema digest, resolved
argument/artifact hashes, destination identity, settings and operation policy.
Validate qualification/authority/freshness at consumption; invoke through existing
GatewayService. The browser only requests the existing permitted action ID.

The backend implementation qualifies explicit version-1
`wright/approved-operation` metadata (effect, destination/file arguments,
structured accepted/rejected status values and provider reference). This is an
optional Wright adapter contract. Missing qualification blocks readiness; it is
not inferred from ordinary MCP tool names or success prose. Source declares exact
connected text/JSON/file argument representations and pins the qualification
digest. Observe mode pins `wright/operation` and each actual status/result/cancel
tool identity before approval. Receipt mode does not imply observed completion.
See [operation evidence/configuration](../evidence/mcp-operations.md) for the
bounded declaration and checked ownership.

Retain local_review/test_handoff aliases and historical records. Test authority
cannot qualify a physical action. Submission accepted, observed start/completion,
rejection, cancellation and unknown outcome are separate recorded receipts/events.
Unknown outcome blocks mutation replay and prompts reconciliation, not blind retry.
Use a nonphysical isolated provider operation for feature acceptance; device/supplier
dispatch needs separate authorization and qualification.

Required checks at implementation

The printed reference can explicitly choose `geometry_operation_mode` as
`ai_task` (default) or `configured_tool` for pinned supplied operations. This
is example preparation using the existing `mcp-tool` argument connection and
source-file dependency contract, not a new runtime mode. Image interpretation
and basis review remain declared work; exact native calls do not receive ignored
image/document ports. Original operation templates are separate frozen review
documents, not run-path configuration used as opaque approval artifacts. The

Explicit `mcp_file_dependencies` are supported on both exact MCP calls and scoped

path, byte count and SHA-256 immediately before consumption. Explicitly supplied
or defaulted prepared file inputs are supported through the same identity check;
they are not represented as tool-produced engineering results. A missing recorded
byte count, changed bytes, mismatched path or unavailable file blocks consumption.
The AI receives
verified locator metadata; binary contents are not loaded as prompt documents.
This declaration does not add tools or widen an agent's capability scope. Plain
AI tasks cannot declare application file imports. Missing, changed or mismatched

Fixed artifact approvals can consume a frozen uploaded or retained file without
regenerating it. Non-local-review approvals require the exact boolean

Absent, false, numeric or string values preserve the existing produced-artifact

Only explicitly connected `WorkflowReference` inputs join the approved artifact
path/hash set. Unrelated workspace files and plain values do not. Prepared binary
files remain opaque; document, mixed-use and MCP argument consumers remain

bytes before decision or after decision prevent dispatch. This declares artifact
scope; it grants no new effect authority and does not classify supplied files as

their separately qualified argument/file contract. Test transport remains an
explicitly enrolled, non-networked simulator.

Coding role

Profile `process-ui-author/1` comprises role name/version, instruction resource
version/hash, model policy (`inherit_default` initially), adapter capability
requirements, allowed artifact scope, permitted tools and repair budget.
Store resolved adapter/model/config identity without credentials on each job.

Extend BaseAgentEngine with backward-compatible optional invocation context and
capability reporting. Hermes must apply effective role/system instructions on
every turn, honor the confined/no-tool first role and inherit the actual default
model. If the underlying platform cannot enforce these constraints, mark authoring
unavailable; do not fall back to broad `/agent/chat` workspace-tool activation.
Do not change a global profile/model for one generation. Future model overrides
and platforms remain capability-checked extensions, not claimed initial support.

Workspace-service authoring job reads the accepted interaction description,
public client/kit docs, template and optional previous UI source. It creates an
isolated session and requests structured source+bindings. Allowed first-role
output is presentation source only; it has no shell, arbitrary filesystem,
engineering MCP or process execution authority. If needed, narrowly scoped
authoring tools go through existing gateway enforcement, not prompt-only permission.

Generation shows resolving/generating/validating/building/preview-ready states and

Source/binding envelope

`wright.process-ui/1` accepts fixed App.tsx, optional style.css, local assets and
binding.json. No package.json, scripts, compiler plugins, backend files, external
URLs, launch argv or environment overrides. Paths must remain under the assigned
revision draft. Initial bounds: 32 source/assets files, 1 MiB total text, 10 MiB
assets, 30 MiB built bundle, 120-second compiler timeout; expose configurable
administrative bounds without allowing model overrides.

Binding manifest fields:

- schema_version, ui_id/revision/parent, title.
- accepted ProcessRef plus interaction-contract major, client/kit supported versions.
- bindings: stable ID; selector kind (input, output role, assessment, interaction,
  observation, action); block/port/role identity; expected schema/version; required

- requested capabilities: closed process operation scopes from the client contract.
- navigation targets and declared result-viewer types.

No credentials, hard-coded run IDs or raw campaign-path naming as authority.
The server compares selectors/types against the accepted process and actual
provider contracts. It grants only configured permitted scopes. Changing a required
binding/schema invalidates compatibility; unresolved optional bindings disclose
fallback. Titles/layout changes do not invalidate engineering output/review.

Preview/save/update API

Routes relative to the existing workspace mount:

| Route suffix | Behavior |
|---|---|
| GET /process-interfaces/authoring-capabilities | Actual role/adapter/model/build readiness and unsupported options |
| POST /process-interfaces/authoring-jobs | Request generation or update for accepted ProcessRef/base revision |
| GET /process-interfaces/authoring-jobs/{job_id} | Durable state, diagnostics and validated preview reference |
| GET /process-interfaces/authoring-jobs/{job_id}/events | Bounded progress/diagnostic event stream |
| POST /process-interfaces/authoring-jobs/{job_id}/cancel | Explicit authoring cancellation |
| POST /process-interfaces/uis/{ui_id}/revisions/{revision_id}/save | Save the built previewed revision using expected hashes |
| POST /process-interfaces/uis/{ui_id}/activate | Select compatible saved revision/rollback |
| GET /process-interfaces/uis/{ui_id}/compatibility | Accepted process/current binding comparison |
| POST /process-interfaces/uis/{ui_id}/present | Resolve saved artifact/grants and create workspace-tab presentation |
| GET /process-interfaces/uis/{ui_id}/runtime-diagnostics | Read exact revision/surface runtime state and bounded existing logs under native process scope |

Runtime diagnostics require `session_id`, `path`, `expected_storage_digest`,
`revision_id` and `surface_id`. The native owner verifies the process/UI and
immutable build provenance, then verifies the existing surface's principal,
workspace, session, Wright ownership and exact revision manifest. Log requests
accept `after_sequence >= 0` and `1 <= limit <= 100`; responses are `no-store`.
This endpoint delegates to the existing runtime/log owners and performs no start,
health probe, generation or process action. It does not change legacy generic
surface principal fallbacks. If the captured buffer is unavailable, persisted
runtime state remains readable with `logs: null` and
`logs_unavailable: "SURFACE_LOGS_UNAVAILABLE"`; this is not evidence that the
original process produced no logs.
After restart, the manager may have no live instance because startup
reconciliation revoked its authority. An exact scoped descriptor remains
readable as `state_source: "surface-reconciliation"`, with `generation` and
`last_health` null and `logs_unavailable: "SURFACE_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND"`.
Its diagnostic summary describes reconciliation, not the original failure or
a new health observation. Live instances use `state_source: "runtime-owner"`.

Preview is read-only against actual references or an explicitly labelled isolated
fixture context. It cannot start work on mount. Saving activates presentation
metadata, not engineering source/evidence. Testing a real process is a separate
explicit operation on the authorized run context.
